patterns.text: Manual talent matching is the operational nerve for B2B service intermediaries dispatching labor on demand. One person typically sources across multiple cities; time-to-hire under 2-3 days is non-negotiable, faster than the manual sourcing layer can sustain.

Vertical operating systems in LATAM (clinical EHRs in health-staffing; customized B2B client platforms in field-services) don't expose APIs. Per-vertical or per-client integration is bespoke. Colombia's national interoperability resolution just launched April 2026; operativization unclear.

Operators in LATAM converge independently on the manifesto thesis 'reemplazar el cómo, no el qué' when discussing AI vs existing systems. They see the value in their existing customer relationships and want to transform internal operations, not be replaced.

Operators in field-services name two unsolved gaps as candidate WTP wedges: (a) self-service contractor onboarding with auto-validation of seguridad social, ARL, certifications, and broker-validated background checks (Rappi-class); (b) pricing intelligence — a contractor-side cost base by activity and city that prevents margin leakage from variable pricing.

The channel landscape these existing businesses operate on is multi-substrate, not WhatsApp-uniform. Customer-facing: WhatsApp dominates in non-regulated verticals (field-services); absent in regulated verticals like health (where operations run on phone + Excel + private EHRs). Contractor-facing: operators select Telegram or other channels even when WhatsApp dominates their customer side. Any agentic system operating these businesses must handle channel multiplicity, not assume a single substrate.

_archived.text: Operators in Colombian health name ambient AI scribes (Digital Environmental Scribes; BMJ Best Practice / UpToDate / DynaMed-class decision-support layer) as the highest-impact, lowest-friction first product to adopt.
Patient cycle-of-attention tracking (alerts on lateral needs without full EHR integration; Tensoreye-class) is the second-most-named high-impact gap.
